# zla_gbrfsx_extended

> Improves the computed solution using extra-precise iterative refinement for complex banded matrices.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zlaGbrfsxExtended from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zla_gbrfsx_extended';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zla_gbrfsx_extended(
    order,
    prec_type,
    trans_type,
    N, kl,
    ku,
    nrhs,
    AB, LDAB,
    AFB, LDAFB,
    IPIV, strideIPIV,
    colequ,
    c, strideC,
    B, LDB,
    Y, LDY,
    BERR_OUT, strideBERR_OUT,
    n_norms,
    ERR_BNDS_NORM, LDERR_BNDS_NORM,
    ERR_BNDS_COMP, LDERR_BNDS_COMP,
    RES, strideRES,
    AYB, strideAYB,
    DY, strideDY,
    Y_TAIL, strideY_TAIL,
    rcond, ithresh, rthresh, dz_ub, ignore_cwise
) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout (`'row-major'` or `'column-major'`) |
| `prec_type` | `integer` | Requested extended-precision type (ignored in this build) |
| `trans_type` | `TransposeOperation` | `'no-transpose'` or `'conjugate-transpose'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix |
| `kl` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of subdiagonals |
| `ku` | `integer` | Number of superdiagonals |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of right-hand sides |
| `AB` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | Input banded matrix |
| ↳ `LDAB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `AB` |
| `AFB` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>LDAF × N</sub> | LU factorization of `AB` |
| ↳ `LDAFB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `AFB` |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Pivot indices (0-based) |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | Stride length for `IPIV` |
| `colequ` | `boolean` | Column-equilibration flag |
| `c` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Column scale factors |
| ↳ `strideC` | `integer` | Stride length for `c` |
| `B` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × nrhs</sub> | Right-hand side matrix |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `B` |
| `Y` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × nrhs</sub> | **in/out** · Current solution matrix (improved on exit) |
| ↳ `LDY` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `Y` |
| `BERR_OUT` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length nrhs</sub> | **out** · Output backward error (length nrhs) |
| ↳ `strideBERR_OUT` | `integer` | Stride length for `BERR_OUT` |
| `n_norms` | `integer` | Number of error bound columns to write |
| `ERR_BNDS_NORM` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>nrhs × N_ERR_BNDS</sub> | **in/out** · Normwise error bounds (nrhs by 3) |
| ↳ `LDERR_BNDS_NORM` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `ERR_BNDS_NORM` |
| `ERR_BNDS_COMP` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>nrhs × N_ERR_BNDS</sub> | **in/out** · Componentwise error bounds (nrhs by 3) |
| ↳ `LDERR_BNDS_COMP` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `ERR_BNDS_COMP` |
| `RES` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Residual workspace (length N) |
| ↳ `strideRES` | `integer` | Stride for `RES` |
| `AYB` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Real workspace `\|A\|*\|Y\|+\|B\|` (length N) |
| ↳ `strideAYB` | `integer` | Stride for `AYB` |
| `DY` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Refinement update workspace (length N) |
| ↳ `strideDY` | `integer` | Stride for `DY` |
| `Y_TAIL` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Extended-precision tail workspace (length N) |
| ↳ `strideY_TAIL` | `integer` | Stride for `Y_TAIL` |
| `rcond` | `number` | Estimate of the reciprocal condition number |
| `ithresh` | `integer` | Maximum number of refinement iterations |
| `rthresh` | `number` | Progress threshold ratio |
| `dz_ub` | `number` | Upper bound on componentwise stopping criterion |
| `ignore_cwise` | `boolean` | Skip componentwise tracking |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `prec_type`: Specifies the intermediate precision to be used in refinement. The value is defined by ILAPREC(P) where P is a CHARACTER and P

  -   = 'S': Single
  -   = 'D': Double
  -   = 'I': Indigenous
  -   = 'X' or 'E': Extra
- `trans_type`: Specifies the transposition operation on A. The value is defined by ILATRANS(T) where T is a CHARACTER and T

  -   = 'N': No transpose
  -   = 'T': Transpose
  -   = 'C': Conjugate transpose
- `N`: The number of linear equations, i.e., the order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `kl`: The number of subdiagonals within the band of A. $\mathrm{KL} \ge 0$.
- `ku`: The number of superdiagonals within the band of A. $\mathrm{KU} \ge 0$
- `nrhs`: The number of right-hand-sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrix B.
- `AB`: On entry, the N-by-N matrix A.
- `AFB`: The factors L and U from the factorization $A = P \, L \, U$ as computed by ZGBTRF.
- `IPIV`: The pivot indices from the factorization $A = P \, L \, U$ as computed by ZGBTRF; row i of the matrix was interchanged with row `IPIV(i)`.
- `colequ`: If .TRUE. then column equilibration was done to A before calling this routine. This is needed to compute the solution and error bounds correctly.
- `c`: The column scale factors for A. If `COLEQU` = .FALSE., C is not accessed. If C is input, each element of C should be a power of the radix to ensure a reliable solution and error estimates. Scaling by powers of the radix does not cause rounding errors unless the result underflows or overflows. Rounding errors during scaling lead to refining with a matrix that is not equivalent to the input matrix, producing error estimates that may not be reliable.
- `B`: The right-hand-side matrix B.
- `Y`: On entry, the solution matrix X, as computed by ZGBTRS. On exit, the improved solution matrix Y.
- `BERR_OUT`: On exit, `BERR_OUT(j)` contains the componentwise relative backward error for right-hand-side j from the formula

  $$
  \max (i) ( \lvert \mathrm{RES}(i) \rvert / ( \lvert \operatorname{op}(\mathrm{A\_s}) \rvert \, \lvert Y \rvert + \lvert \mathrm{B\_s} \rvert )(i) )
  $$

  where abs(Z) is the componentwise absolute value of the matrix or vector Z. This is computed by ZLA\_LIN\_BERR.
- `n_norms`: Determines which error bounds to return (see `ERR_BNDS_NORM` and `ERR_BNDS_COMP`). If $\mathrm{N\_NORMS} \ge 1$ return normwise error bounds. If $\mathrm{N\_NORMS} \ge 2$ return componentwise error bounds.
- `ERR_BNDS_NORM`: For each right-hand side, this array contains information about various error bounds and condition numbers corresponding to the normwise relative error, which is defined as follows:

  Normwise relative error in the ith solution vector:

  max\_j (abs(XTRUE(j,i) - X(j,i))) ------------------------------ max\_j abs(X(j,i))

  The array is indexed by the type of error information as described below. There currently are up to three pieces of information returned.

  The first index in `ERR_BNDS_NORM(i,:)` corresponds to the ith right-hand side.

  The second index in `ERR_BNDS_NORM(:,err)` contains the following three fields: err = 1 "Trust/don't trust" boolean. Trust the answer if the

  -   reciprocal condition number is less than the threshold
  -   sqrt(n) \* slamch('Epsilon').

  err = 2 "Guaranteed" error bound: The estimated forward error,

  -   almost certainly within a factor of 10 of the true error
  -   so long as the next entry is greater than the threshold
  -   sqrt(n) \* slamch('Epsilon'). This error bound should only
  -   be trusted if the previous boolean is true.

  err = 3 Reciprocal condition number: Estimated normwise

  -   reciprocal condition number. Compared with the threshold
  -   sqrt(n) \* slamch('Epsilon') to determine if the error
  -   estimate is "guaranteed". These reciprocal condition
  -   numbers are 1 / (norm(Z^{-1},inf) \* norm(Z,inf)) for some
  -   appropriately scaled matrix Z.
  -   Let $Z = S \, A$, where S scales each row by a power of the
  -   radix so all absolute row sums of Z are approximately 1.

  This subroutine is only responsible for setting the second field above. See Lapack Working Note 165 for further details and extra cautions.
- `ERR_BNDS_COMP`: For each right-hand side, this array contains information about various error bounds and condition numbers corresponding to the componentwise relative error, which is defined as follows:

  Componentwise relative error in the ith solution vector:

  abs(XTRUE(j,i) - X(j,i)) max\_j ---------------------- abs(X(j,i))

  The array is indexed by the right-hand side i (on which the componentwise relative error depends), and the type of error information as described below. There currently are up to three pieces of information returned for each right-hand side. If componentwise accuracy is not requested (PARAMS(3) = 0.0), then `ERR_BNDS_COMP` is not accessed. If $\mathrm{N\_ERR\_BNDS} < 3$, then at most the first (:,N\_ERR\_BNDS) entries are returned.

  The first index in `ERR_BNDS_COMP(i,:)` corresponds to the ith right-hand side.

  The second index in `ERR_BNDS_COMP(:,err)` contains the following three fields: err = 1 "Trust/don't trust" boolean. Trust the answer if the

  -   reciprocal condition number is less than the threshold
  -   sqrt(n) \* slamch('Epsilon').

  err = 2 "Guaranteed" error bound: The estimated forward error,

  -   almost certainly within a factor of 10 of the true error
  -   so long as the next entry is greater than the threshold
  -   sqrt(n) \* slamch('Epsilon'). This error bound should only
  -   be trusted if the previous boolean is true.

  err = 3 Reciprocal condition number: Estimated componentwise

  -   reciprocal condition number. Compared with the threshold
  -   sqrt(n) \* slamch('Epsilon') to determine if the error
  -   estimate is "guaranteed". These reciprocal condition
  -   numbers are 1 / (norm(Z^{-1},inf) \* norm(Z,inf)) for some
  -   appropriately scaled matrix Z.
  -   Let $Z = S \, (A \, \operatorname{diag}(x))$, where x is the solution for the
  -   current right-hand side and S scales each row of
  -   $A \, \operatorname{diag}(x)$ by a power of the radix so all absolute row
  -   sums of Z are approximately 1.

  This subroutine is only responsible for setting the second field above. See Lapack Working Note 165 for further details and extra cautions.
- `RES`: Workspace to hold the intermediate residual.
- `AYB`: Workspace.
- `DY`: Workspace to hold the intermediate solution.
- `Y_TAIL`: Workspace to hold the trailing bits of the intermediate solution.
- `rcond`: Reciprocal scaled condition number. This is an estimate of the reciprocal Skeel condition number of the matrix A after equilibration (if done). If this is less than the machine precision (in particular, if it is zero), the matrix is singular to working precision. Note that the error may still be small even if this number is very small and the matrix appears ill- conditioned.
- `ithresh`: The maximum number of residual computations allowed for refinement. The default is 10. For 'aggressive' set to 100 to permit convergence using approximate factorizations or factorizations other than LU. If the factorization uses a technique other than Gaussian elimination, the guarantees in `ERR_BNDS_NORM` and `ERR_BNDS_COMP` may no longer be trustworthy.
- `rthresh`: Determines when to stop refinement if the error estimate stops decreasing. Refinement will stop when the next solution no longer satisfies norm(dx\_{i+1}) \< `RTHRESH` \* norm(dx\_i) where norm(Z) is the infinity norm of Z. `RTHRESH` satisfies $0 < \mathrm{RTHRESH} \le 1$. The default value is 0.5. For 'aggressive' set to 0.9 to permit convergence on extremely ill-conditioned matrices. See LAWN 165 for more details.
- `dz_ub`: Determines when to start considering componentwise convergence. Componentwise convergence is only considered after each component of the solution Y is stable, which we define as the relative change in each component being less than `DZ_UB`. The default value is 0.25, requiring the first bit to be stable. See LAWN 165 for more details.
- `ignore_cwise`: If .TRUE. then ignore componentwise convergence. Default value is .FALSE..

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid transpose operation
- `RangeError` `N` must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` ninth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` eleventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` eighteenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` twentieth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` twenty-fifth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` twenty-seventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zla_gbrfsx_extended.strided(
    prec_type,
    trans_type,
    N, kl,
    ku,
    nrhs,
    AB, strideAB1, strideAB2, offsetAB,
    AFB, strideAFB1, strideAFB2, offsetAFB,
    IPIV, strideIPIV, offsetIPIV,
    colequ,
    c, strideC, offsetC,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB,
    Y, strideY1, strideY2, offsetY,
    BERR_OUT, strideBERR_OUT, offsetBERR_OUT,
    n_norms,
    ERR_BNDS_NORM, strideERR_BNDS_NORM1, strideERR_BNDS_NORM2, offsetERR_BNDS_NORM,
    ERR_BNDS_COMP, strideERR_BNDS_COMP1, strideERR_BNDS_COMP2, offsetERR_BNDS_COMP,
    RES, strideRES, offsetRES,
    AYB, strideAYB, offsetAYB,
    DY, strideDY, offsetDY,
    Y_TAIL, strideY_TAIL, offsetY_TAIL,
    rcond, ithresh, rthresh, dz_ub, ignore_cwise
) → integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `prec_type` | `integer` | Requested extended-precision type (ignored in this build) |
| `trans_type` | `TransposeOperation` | `'no-transpose'` or `'conjugate-transpose'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix |
| `kl` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of subdiagonals |
| `ku` | `integer` | Number of superdiagonals |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of right-hand sides |
| `AB` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | Input banded matrix |
| ↳ `strideAB1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `AB` |
| ↳ `strideAB2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `AB` |
| ↳ `offsetAB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `AB` |
| `AFB` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>LDAF × N</sub> | LU factorization of `AB` |
| ↳ `strideAFB1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `AFB` |
| ↳ `strideAFB2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `AFB` |
| ↳ `offsetAFB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `AFB` |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Pivot indices (0-based) |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | Stride length for `IPIV` |
| ↳ `offsetIPIV` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `IPIV` |
| `colequ` | `boolean` | Column-equilibration flag |
| `c` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Column scale factors |
| ↳ `strideC` | `integer` | Stride length for `c` |
| ↳ `offsetC` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `c` |
| `B` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × nrhs</sub> | Right-hand side matrix |
| ↳ `strideB1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `B` |
| ↳ `strideB2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `B` |
| ↳ `offsetB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `B` |
| `Y` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × nrhs</sub> | **in/out** · Current solution matrix (improved on exit) |
| ↳ `strideY1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `Y` |
| ↳ `strideY2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `Y` |
| ↳ `offsetY` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `Y` |
| `BERR_OUT` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length nrhs</sub> | **out** · Output backward error (length nrhs) |
| ↳ `strideBERR_OUT` | `integer` | Stride length for `BERR_OUT` |
| ↳ `offsetBERR_OUT` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `BERR_OUT` |
| `n_norms` | `integer` | Number of error bound columns to write |
| `ERR_BNDS_NORM` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>nrhs × N_ERR_BNDS</sub> | **in/out** · Normwise error bounds (nrhs by 3) |
| ↳ `strideERR_BNDS_NORM1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension |
| ↳ `strideERR_BNDS_NORM2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension |
| ↳ `offsetERR_BNDS_NORM` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index |
| `ERR_BNDS_COMP` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>nrhs × N_ERR_BNDS</sub> | **in/out** · Componentwise error bounds (nrhs by 3) |
| ↳ `strideERR_BNDS_COMP1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension |
| ↳ `strideERR_BNDS_COMP2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension |
| ↳ `offsetERR_BNDS_COMP` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index |
| `RES` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Residual workspace (length N) |
| ↳ `strideRES` | `integer` | Stride for `RES` |
| ↳ `offsetRES` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `RES` |

| `rcond` | `number` | Estimate of the reciprocal condition number |
| `ithresh` | `integer` | Maximum number of refinement iterations |
| `rthresh` | `number` | Progress threshold ratio |
| `dz_ub` | `number` | Upper bound on componentwise stopping criterion |
| `ignore_cwise` | `boolean` | Skip componentwise tracking |

  -   sums of Z are approximately 1.

  This subroutine is only responsible for setting the second field above. See Lapack Working Note 165 for further details and extra cautions.
- `RES`: Workspace to hold the intermediate residual.
- `AYB`: Workspace.
- `DY`: Workspace to hold the intermediate solution.
- `Y_TAIL`: Workspace to hold the trailing bits of the intermediate solution.
- `rcond`: Reciprocal scaled condition number. This is an estimate of the reciprocal Skeel condition number of the matrix A after equilibration (if done). If this is less than the machine precision (in particular, if it is zero), the matrix is singular to working precision. Note that the error may still be small even if this number is very small and the matrix appears ill- conditioned.
- `ithresh`: The maximum number of residual computations allowed for refinement. The default is 10. For 'aggressive' set to 100 to permit convergence using approximate factorizations or factorizations other than LU. If the factorization uses a technique other than Gaussian elimination, the guarantees in `ERR_BNDS_NORM` and `ERR_BNDS_COMP` may no longer be trustworthy.
- `rthresh`: Determines when to stop refinement if the error estimate stops decreasing. Refinement will stop when the next solution no longer satisfies norm(dx\_{i+1}) \< `RTHRESH` \* norm(dx\_i) where norm(Z) is the infinity norm of Z. `RTHRESH` satisfies $0 < \mathrm{RTHRESH} \le 1$. The default value is 0.5. For 'aggressive' set to 0.9 to permit convergence on extremely ill-conditioned matrices. See LAWN 165 for more details.
- `dz_ub`: Determines when to start considering componentwise convergence. Componentwise convergence is only considered after each component of the solution Y is stable, which we define as the relative change in each component being less than `DZ_UB`. The default value is 0.25, requiring the first bit to be stable. See LAWN 165 for more details.
- `ignore_cwise`: If .TRUE. then ignore componentwise convergence. Default value is .FALSE..

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid transpose operation
- `RangeError` `N` and `nrhs` must be nonnegative integers

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `info !== 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: Successful exit.
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the ith argument to ZGBTRS had an illegal value

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `zla_gbrfsx_extended()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZLA_GBRFSX_EXTENDED`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/zla_gbrfsx_extended.f).
-   Extended-precision residual paths (`BLAS_ZGBMV_X`, `BLAS_ZGBMV2_X`) are not available in this build; the routine always uses the standard `zgbmv` residual. The `prec_type` parameter is accepted for API compatibility but has no effect.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
/* eslint-disable camelcase, max-len */

import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import zla_gbrfsx_extended from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zla_gbrfsx_extended';

// 2x2 diagonal complex system (KL=KU=0) with an exact initial solution Y.
const N = 2;
const KL = 0;
const KU = 0;
const LDAB = 1;
const LDAFB = 1;

const AB = new Complex128Array( [ 2.0, 0.0, 3.0, 0.0 ] );
const AFB = new Complex128Array( [ 2.0, 0.0, 3.0, 0.0 ] );
const IPIV = new Int32Array( [ 0, 1 ] );
const B = new Complex128Array( [ 2.0, 0.0, 3.0, 0.0 ] );
const Y = new Complex128Array( [ 1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.0 ] );
const RES = new Complex128Array( N );
const DY = new Complex128Array( N );
const Y_TAIL = new Complex128Array( N );
const C = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 1.0 ] );
const AYB = new Float64Array( N );
const BERR_OUT = new Float64Array( 1 );
const ERR_BNDS_NORM = new Float64Array( 3 );
const ERR_BNDS_COMP = new Float64Array( 3 );
ERR_BNDS_NORM[ 0 ] = 1.0;
ERR_BNDS_COMP[ 0 ] = 1.0;

zla_gbrfsx_extended( 'column-major', 1, 'no-transpose', N, KL, KU, 1, AB, LDAB, AFB, LDAFB, IPIV, 1, false, C, 1, B, N, Y, N, BERR_OUT, 1, 2, ERR_BNDS_NORM, 1, ERR_BNDS_COMP, 1, RES, 1, AYB, 1, DY, 1, Y_TAIL, 1, 1.0, 10, 0.5, 0.25, false );

console.log( BERR_OUT ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZLA_GBRFSX_EXTENDED`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZLA\_GBRFSX\_EXTENDED improves the computed solution to a system of linear equations by performing extra-precise iterative refinement and provides error bounds and backward error estimates for the solution. This subroutine is called by ZGBRFSX to perform iterative refinement. In addition to normwise error bound, the code provides maximum componentwise error bound if possible. See comments for `ERR_BNDS_NORM` and `ERR_BNDS_COMP` for details of the error bounds. Note that this subroutine is only responsible for setting the second fields of `ERR_BNDS_NORM` and `ERR_BNDS_COMP`.

</section>
